title: Subtrusive topology, stability, and detection of quasi-compactness
statement: Work over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Quasi-compactness of a space means that every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source. A space is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact, and a morphism is quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. The constructible topology of a scheme is locally generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements; on a space it is the quotient topology from representable etale affine scheme charts. A map $a:X\to Y$ is universally subtrusive if, after every affine scheme base change $T\to Y$, it is surjective and quotient in the constructible topology and each specialization pair $t_0\in\overline{\{t_1\}}$ lifts to a specialization pair in $X\times_YT$. For morphisms of quasi-separated spaces: (1) a universally subtrusive map is universally submersive in the Zariski topology: every algebraic-space base change is a surjective quotient map; the affine scheme tests in the definition suffice. Universally subtrusive maps are stable under arbitrary base change between quasi-separated spaces and under composition. If a composite $X\to Y\to Z$ is universally subtrusive, its second factor $Y\to Z$ is universally subtrusive. (2) Every universally open surjective map is universally subtrusive; in particular this holds for a surjective representable etale map. (3) If $a:Y'\to Y$ is universally subtrusive and $b:Z\to Y$ is a morphism between quasi-separated spaces, then $b$ is quasi-compact if and only if $Z\times_YY'\to Y'$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Rydh (author version 2010-03-03), Corollary (1.5), Proposition (1.7)(iii), Remark (1.8), Definition (2.2), the paragraph preceding Proposition (2.4), Proposition (2.4)(ii), and Remark (2.5)(2c); printed pp.5--8. Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: All fibre products used below remain quasi-separated. Here is the affine-test verification, so no finiteness of the base changes is assumed. For $P=X\times_YW$ and affine schemes $U,V\to P$, put $D_X=U\times_XV$ and $D_W=U\times_WV$. These are quasi-compact schemes by quasi-separatedness of $X,W$ (the affine-test characterization in [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-fibre-product]). Each maps monomorphically to the affine scheme $U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}V$, hence is separated over it: the relative diagonal of a monomorphism is an isomorphism. Thus these schemes are quasi-separated. The sheaf identity $U\times_PV=D_X\times_{U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}V}D_W$ follows on sections by requiring equality of the two projections. Apply [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-fibre-product] to its three qcqs factors (the ambient affine scheme is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]). It is quasi-compact, proving the required absolute-diagonal condition for $P$. The same argument applies to all iterated products.

source.place: Terminology and assumptions, printed p.4: all spaces quasi-separated; routine diagonal verification for the products in (1.7) and (2.2).

proof.text: First consider a map $f:X\to T$ satisfying the two subtrusive conditions over an affine scheme $T$. It is surjective by hypothesis. If $F\subseteq|T|$ has Zariski closed inverse image, that inverse image is constructible-topology closed by [lem-sfb-space-constructible-topology-comparison]. The constructible quotient condition makes $F$ constructible-topology closed. Given $t_1\in F$ and $t_0\in\overline{\{t_1\}}$, lift the pair to $x_0\in\overline{\{x_1\}}$. Since $x_1\in f^{-1}F$ and the latter is closed, $x_0\in f^{-1}F$, hence $t_0\in F$. The closedness criterion of [lem-sfb-space-constructible-topology-comparison] now makes $F$ Zariski closed. Conversely a closed $F$ has closed inverse image by the point-map continuity of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. This proves the Zariski quotient assertion over every affine test.

source.place: Corollary (1.5), Proposition (2.1)(i), Definition (2.2), and paragraph preceding (2.4).

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ satisfy the affine tests of the statement and let $W\to Y$ be any quasi-separated algebraic-space base change. Write $P=X\times_YW$. Choose a surjective etale presentation by affine charts $u_i:U_i\to W$ using [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. For a subset $F\subseteq|W|$ with closed inverse image in $P$ (in either the Zariski or constructible topology), its inverse image in $P\times_WU_i$ is closed by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] or [lem-sfb-space-constructible-topology-comparison]. Over $U_i$ the affine-test quotient condition, or step 2, gives closed $u_i^{-1}F$. The final-topology definition of [def-a1-space-point-topology] or the presentation clause of [lem-sfb-space-constructible-topology-comparison] makes $F$ closed in $W$. Surjectivity persists by the image formula in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Thus $P\to W$ is quotient in both topologies. A specialization $w_0\in\overline{\{w_1\}}$ lifts to a pair in a single $U_i$: choose a point over $w_0$ and use [lem-sfb-open-space-generization-lifting] on the open chart map to lift $w_1$. The affine test over $U_i$ lifts that pair to $P\times_WU_i$, and projection to $P$ preserves specialization. Consequently the subtrusive conditions hold over every such $W$, not just schemes. Reapplying the affine test with a composite $T\to W\to Y$ proves arbitrary base-change stability.

source.place: Remark (1.8), Definition (2.2), Proposition (2.4)(ii), and end of section 2. The chart maps are open by Stacks 03IR, in the cited point-calculus statement.

proof.text: For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ universally subtrusive, base change to an affine $T\to Z$. Step 3 applies to $f$ over $Y_T$, and the test for $g$ applies over $T$. Composing surjective quotient maps is quotient: a subset has closed inverse image under the composite exactly when its inverse image under the second map is closed, exactly when it is closed. Lift a pair in $T$ first to $Y_T$, then to $X_T$. This proves composition. If instead only $gf$ is universally subtrusive, its point surjectivity implies that of $g_T$. A subset with closed inverse image under $g_T$ has closed inverse image under $(gf)_T$, by constructible continuity of $f_T$ from [lem-sfb-space-constructible-topology-comparison]; hence it is closed in $T$. The reverse implication is continuity. A pair lifted to $X_T$ projects to a pair in $Y_T$ by Zariski continuity [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Thus the second factor satisfies every affine test, proving the right-factor assertion.

source.place: Paragraph preceding Proposition (2.4): composition and right factors; Definition (2.2).

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ be universally open and surjective; this means that each algebraic-space base change is open on point spaces. Fix affine $T\to Y$. Surjectivity of $f_T$ follows from [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Choose affine etale charts $U_i\to X_T$ by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Their composites to $T$ are open by point calculus and openness of $f_T$. Their images cover $T$, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] supplies finitely many whose images cover $T$. Their disjoint union $U$ is a scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and is quasi-compact (a finite union of quasi-compact affine components) and quasi-separated: the absolute diagonal restricts to the affine-component diagonals on same-component products and to the empty map on different-component products. Its map $U\to T$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]. By [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-constructible-closed] it is constructible closed, and it is surjective, hence constructible quotient: if the inverse image of $F$ is closed, its image is $F$. As it factors through $X_T$, constructible continuity from [lem-sfb-space-constructible-topology-comparison] implies that $f_T$ is also quotient. Finally choose $x_0$ over $t_0$ and apply [lem-sfb-open-space-generization-lifting] to the open map $f_T$ to lift each generalization $t_1$ of $t_0$. This proves subtrusiveness on every affine test.

source.place: Proposition (1.6)(iii), proof, and Remark (2.5)(2c): finite quasi-compact source refinement over an affine target, then generization lifting.

proof.text: A surjective representable etale morphism stays representable etale and surjective after arbitrary base change by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Its point map is open by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. It is therefore universally open and surjective, and step 5 applies.

source.place: Remark (2.5)(2c); etale openness is Stacks 03IR, stated in point calculus.

proof.text: For (3), the forward implication is base-change stability of quasi-compactness [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. Conversely assume $b':Z\times_YY'\to Y'$ is quasi-compact. Fix affine $T\to Y$ and set $V=Z\times_YT$, $Q=Y'\times_YT$, $V'=V\times_TQ$, with maps $f:V\to T$, $a_T:Q\to T$, $f':V'\to Q$, and $p:V'\to V$. The map $f'$ is a base change of $b'$, hence quasi-compact by the same node, so constructible closed by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-constructible-closed]. If $F$ is constructible closed in $V$, then $p^{-1}F$ is closed by [lem-sfb-space-constructible-topology-comparison]. The point image identity of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives $a_T^{-1}(f(F))=f'(p^{-1}F)$: any pair of points of $V,Q$ over the same point of $T$ lifts to $V'$. The right side is closed. The affine subtrusive test makes $a_T$ constructible quotient, so $f(F)$ is closed. Thus $f$ is constructible closed.

source.place: Proposition (1.7)(iii), proof: descend constructible closedness via the image identity of (1.7)(i); Remark (1.8).

proof.text: Each point fibre of $f$ is quasi-compact in the constructible topology as a subspace of $V$. To verify this, let $t\in T$, represented by $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ with $K=\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Surjectivity of $Q\to T$ gives a field extension $L/K$ and a lift $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Q$ (use the common-field-extension definition [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]). The base change of $f'$ over this affine field scheme has source $V_L$ quasi-compact by its quasi-compactness. The projection $V_L\to V_K$ is surjective and continuous by the same point-calculus image formula, since $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is surjective. Thus $V_K$ is quasi-compact: pull an open cover back to $V_L$ and take its finite subcover. Choose an affine surjective etale $U\to V_K$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. The constructible point space of $U$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral], and [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-quasi-compact]. The composite $|U|_{\rm cons}\to|V_K|_{\rm cons}\to|V|_{\rm cons}$ is continuous by [lem-sfb-space-constructible-topology-comparison]. Its image is exactly $f^{-1}(t)$, by the fibre-product point-image formula. A continuous image of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact, by pulling back any open cover. This proves the claim, including empty fibres.

source.place: Proposition (1.7)(iii), proof: quasi-compactness of fibres and their constructible images; EGA I 7.2.13(i) replaced by the cited affine-atlas compactness argument.

proof.text: Here is the remaining topological compactness argument explicitly. The constructible topology of affine $T$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral], and [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-quasi-compact]. Given a constructible-open cover of $V$, for every $t$ choose finitely many members covering $f^{-1}(t)$ by step 8, and call their union $O_t$. Since $f$ is closed by step 7, $N_t=T\setminus f(V\setminus O_t)$ is constructible open, contains $t$, and satisfies $f^{-1}N_t\subseteq O_t$. The $N_t$ cover $T$, so finitely many suffice. The finitely many corresponding finite families of original cover members cover $V$. Thus $V$ is constructible quasi-compact, hence Zariski quasi-compact since the constructible topology is finer by [lem-sfb-space-constructible-topology-comparison]. This works for every affine $T\to Y$, so it is precisely quasi-compactness of $b$ as defined in the statement. If $T$ is empty the cover and conclusion are empty and the same argument applies.

source.place: Proposition (1.7)(iii), final proper-map argument, expanded on affine tests instead of citing EGA I 7.2.13(v).

proof_origin.place: Expanded Rydh (1.5)--(1.8), (2.2), paragraph before (2.4), (2.4)(ii), and (2.5)(2c), read online; local copy WANTED. The fibre-compactness and closed-map compactness arguments are written out using existing DAG inputs.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NL-9d62e4a36 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and all three new nodes in full, the full statement of every cited node, and the parent lem-sfb-space-qc-subtrusive-etale-descent (steps 2, 5, 8 and 10 cite the item: submersive, right factor, composition, open surjective). The Rydh PDF is not in literature/ (same WANTED gap as the parent), so I checked every statement mathematically myself, using local Stacks 040F, 0903, 054I and 0ECW. Step 1: U×_P V = (U×_X V)×_{U×V}(U×_W V); each factor is qc by the affine-test form of quasi-separated, and separated because it is mono into an affine. Step 2: specialization stability plus the 0903 criterion. Step 3: an affine presentation, with generization lifting along the open chart so the lift stays in one affine chart. Step 4: composition, and the right factor via constructible-topology continuity of f_T. Step 5: finitely many chart images cover T, the finite coproduct is qcqs, so it is constructible-closed, hence a quotient. Step 6: étale permanence. Step 7: a_T^{-1}f(F)=f'(p^{-1}F). Step 8: fibre over κ(t)⊆L, V_L qc ⇒ V_K qc ⇒ affine atlas ⇒ spectral ⇒ compact, with image exactly f^{-1}(t). Step 9: the tube argument. The new nodes are true. Comparison: presentation independence for qs spaces, continuity, finer topology, 0903 on charts. Constructible-closed: compact-to-Hausdorff argument on charts, and the qc hypothesis is needed (an infinite set of closed points in A^1 fails without it). Generization lifting: 040F for schemes; for qs spaces via the limit Spec O_{U,x0} and compact fibres. Each new node is strictly smaller than the item, restates no clause of it, and is not a duplicate of the space-étale lifting nodes, the spectral nodes or any blueprint node. Batch-5 flags: the trf/a1 citations are generic algebraic-space definitions and foundations, outside the trace-formula and Poincaré assumptions, so they are accepted. Tool uses for lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover, lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus and lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests are accepted as generic. No SGA. No changes.

reviewed_lean.note: All 9 theorems match the node clause by clause: (1) universally subtrusive implies universally submersive over any space base change, affine tests suffice for both properties, stable under base change between quasi-separated spaces and under composition, second factor of a universally subtrusive composite (no surjectivity of f assumed); (2) universally open surjective, and representable etale surjective, imply universally subtrusive; (3) MapIsQuasiCompact b iff MapIsQuasiCompact of pullback.snd b a. Only IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated on every space; no extra hypotheses; one universe u. New def nodes are not hollow: pointConstructibleTopology is the supremum of coinduced Mathlib constructibleTopology over etale affine charts (the final topology, same pattern as the live pointTopologicalSpace); MapIsSubtrusive is IsQuotientMap (includes surjectivity) plus specialization-pair lifting in the correct direction; universal versions are as the node states. Item changes only lean and stmt_deps (5 definition nodes added, all used); 6 dependency records byte-identical to side-live; statement fields verbatim; docstrings carry sources and proof plans; sorry only.
